full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J : This appeal by leave at the instance of the defendant is directed against the judgment and order of a Division Bench of the High Court Division passed on 4.9.94 in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 95 of 1993 allowing the appeal, after setting aside the judgment and order dated 10.3.93 passed by the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.2 in Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1992 under section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure and directing that the Miscellaneous Case No.275 of 1992 be tried analogously with Title Suit No. 177 of 1984 (renumbered as Title Suit No. 255 of.l985 now Title Suit No. 212 of 1994). 

 2. Appellant Mrs. Shahana Hossain was a defendant in Title Suit No.l77 of 1984 in the Fourth Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The suit was for specific performance of contract for sale of house at Pallabi, Dhaka. On transfer to the Court of 2nd Subordinate Judge, Dhaka the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 255 of 1985. The suit was decreed ex parte in favour of the plaintiff-respondent. In Title Execution Case No. 95 of 1985 of the Fourth Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The respondent obtained possession of the suit house by evicting the appellant on 31st July, 1986. At the instance of the appellant the ex parte decree was set aside on 26 May, 1990 with a direction for the restoration of the suit. On 7.1.91 the" appellant filed an application under section 144 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Artha Rin Adalat vide judgment and order dated 10.3.93 in Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1992 dismissed the appellant's case for restitution and damages. Aggrieved by that order the appellant filed FMA No. 95 of 1993 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and order dated 10th March, 1993. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Judges of the High Court Division were legally justified in directing analogous disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1992 for restitution of possession under section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure with Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 in which the appellant was a defendant after holding that the trial Court dismissed the miscellaneous case on an erroneous view of law and thereby illegally refused restitution of the suit property to the appellant which she is entitled to get back under the law. 

 5. It may be stated that the learned Judges of the High Court Division wrongly used the words "for doing complete justice" between the parties. Under the Constitution it is only the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court which has got the power under Article" 104 of the Constitution to issue such directions, orders, decrees or writs as may be necessary for doing complete justice in any matter pending before it. This power of doing complete justice, strictly speaking, does not rest with the other courts. Probably in this case due to the circumstances that the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing on 4.10.94, the learned Judges deciding the appeal on 4.9.94 thought it fit and proper to direct the disposal of the miscellaneous case along with the suit. The material question that is to be decided in this appeal is what will be the legal effect of an application filed under section 144 of the Code for restitution of possession when the application is legally maintainable and the appellant is lawfully entitled to possession. 

 6. As already noticed, in Title Suit No. 177 of 1984 the suit was decreed ex parte in favour of the plaintiff-respondent and in Title Execution Case No. 95 of 1985 the respondent obtained possession of the suit house by evicting the appellant on 31 July, 1986. At the instance of the appellant the ex parte decree was set aside with a direction for restoration of the suit and the appellant filed an application under Section 144 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for possession. According to plain reading of section 144 of the Code, the decree having been varied or reversed the court of first instance shall on application of any party entitled to any benefit by way of restitution or otherwise is entitled to possession. This being the mandate of law and the learned Judges of the High Court Division having clearly held that the dismissal of the miscellaneous case was made on an erroneous view of law the appellant is entitled to get back the possession of the suit property. He has been dispossessed in execution of an ex parte decree which no longer remains in force. The same has been set aside by a competent court of law. The appellant is entitled to possession. The order of analogous trial of the Miscellaneous case with the Title Suit in fact amounts to refusal of restitution of possession and the Miscellaneous case is thus unnecessarily kept alive by the High Court Division although it was dismissed by the learned Subordinate Judge. The grant of restitution is not discretionary with the court, but law imposes an obligation on the party who gets the benefit of a varied or reversed decree to make restitution to the other party for his loss:
